answer:
A poor scanned, image-only PDF blocks go-live through the following chain:

1. **Ingestion failure**: The current ingestion pipeline relies on standard PDF text extraction, so an image-only PDF has no detectable text layer, leading to an empty document model and empty index [NL-029-S05]. KnowledgeHub cannot extract text from these files without advanced OCR, causing failed or incomplete ingestion [NL-010-S06]. The standard PDF parser fails on image-only documents, producing empty indexes unless external OCR pre-processing is applied [NL-031-S04].

2. **Retrieval and citation degradation**: Because no text is indexed, TutorChat either misses the content entirely or returns incomplete answers [NL-018-S05]. When it does answer from such files, it either returns no source citations because it cannot find text offsets, or it cites the entire document (e.g., page 1 of a 250-page PDF) instead of the exact section [NL-021-S02]. This violates reliability guidelines [NL-021-S02].

3. **Reliability gate failure**: Scanned PDFs return incomplete citations, failing the go-live validation threshold that requires 85% citation correctness [NL-031-S04]. Compliance officers then refuse to sign off on rollout; for example, BrightPath Healthcare remained restricted to its 100-user pilot and could not expand to 6,500 employees until the citation issue was solved [NL-021-S02].

4. **Manual OCR workaround delays go-live**: The temporary workaround — manual external OCR pre-processing and verification — adds weeks to onboarding, e.g., Northstar Financial’s pilot was delayed by three weeks [NL-010-S06], and BrightPath’s manual formatting checks on scanned compliance files produced the longest onboarding time at 9.5 weeks [NL-031-S04], preventing timely go-live.
